page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with marginal notes in the left and right margins. Left margin: "NB." beside the line "quit Theophylactus"; "Melarti-ficiale." beside "de melle historia" and "Apollonium referre". Right margin: a small mark beside "modo" (probably a stain). Catchword at the lower right below the last line.

main_text.p: Democritus quoque Abderides fenex,[?] interrogatus, quanam ratione quispiam sane degeret, respondit, si interiora melle, exteriora oleo madefierent, melle enim ipsum plurimum delectatum tradunt, sicut & Pythagoram, qui cum frugalissime viveret, solo sæpe melle fuit contentus.

Cyrnios Sardiniam incolentes ideo diutius viuere quidam tradiderunt, quod ipsis mel perpetuum erat escarium. Valleriola in locis suis comm.l.3. melle, ob detergendi calefaciendiq; potestatem insignem, lenibus plurimo utendum consulit, si modo illæsam lenectam in multum æui producere velint, idque probat Antiochi Medici & Telephi Grammatici exemplo, qui senes annosi, attico melle & pane plurimum vtebantur, Gal.f.de sanctuenda teste. Quin & ipse Saluator Christus à mellis usu non abstinuit, testatur enim Lucas spectantibus post resurrectionem discipulis ipsum de mellis suo comedisse, non quidem φυσικῶς, ut inquit Theophylactus, cibo enim non amplius indigebat, sed οἰκονομικῶς, nempe resurrectionis, & veri sui corporis confirmandi gratia. NB.Non omittendum autem in hac de melle historia, Eudoxum Cindium apud Apollonium referre, in Aphrica quandam gentem esse, quæ supra Syrtes & Chartagi-Melarti-ficiale.

page.notes: The page number is printed as "s88"; the first figure looks like a long s, read as 588 with [?]. The right margin mark beside "modo" looks like a stain, not a note. The catchword "nem" completes "Chartaginem". Several words in the Greek and in the Latin of the first lines are small and faint; "fenex," and "sanctuenda" (rendered as printed, "sanctuenda teste"?) are doubtful. "Gal.f.de sanctuenda teste" was printed in running text and is uncertain. Some letters in the Latin are blurred, especially at the right edge of the page.
